textbookText: i. They were 4.5 feet tall with erect posture more like a man and were omnivorous. ii. Its brain capacity was between 650-800 c.c. iii. H. habilis (habilis = mentally able or skillful) were the first to make tools mainly out of chipped stones.
Figure: 7.4.7 Homo habilis 5. Homo erectus (Erect man)

They appeared about 1.5 million years ago in the middle pleistocene. H. erectus evolved from H. habilis. They had erect posture with 900 cc of cranial capacity. They had protruding jaws, projecting brow ridges and small canines and large molar teeth. They might have consumed meat. They made more elaborate tools of stones and bones, hunted big game and perhaps knew and used fire. Two fossils of similar type were discovered at Java (Africa) and Peking (China).

Figure: 7.4.8 Homo erectus H. erectus includes Java man, Peking man and Heidelberg man. (i) Java man (Pithecanthropus or Homo erectus erectus): Eugene Dubols discovered its fossil from pleistocene rocks in central Java (Island of Indonesia) and named it Pithecanthropus erectus. They existed 50,000 years ago.
Some of its characteristic features are listed below: i. They had a brain of 900 c.c. capacity. ii. They were taller than 5 feet. iii. They lacked a distinct chin but had eye ridges.

iv. They are believed to be the first prehistoric man to use fire for hunting, defense and cooking food. v. They were omnivorous in their feeding habit, having meat as the chief diet. (ii) Peking Man (Sinanthropus or Homo erectus pekinensis) Peking men were very similar to Java men. Their fossils were recovered by W.C. Pel from the limestone caves near Peking and named them Sinanthropus. Later, Mayer renamed it H. erectus pekinensis.

Some of its characteristic features are listed below: i. They were around 5 feet tall. ii. Their bodies were lighter and weaker than Java men. iii. They had a brain of 900 -1200 c.c. capacity. iv. They had undeveloped chin but had developed eye ridges. v. They used relatively sophisticated sharp tools made of stones for hunting animals for food and defence. They were cannibals too.
(iii) Heidelberg man (Homo erectus heldelbergensis) The fossil (jaw) of H. erectus heldelbergensis was discovered in Heidelberg, Germany. It is supposed to be the ancestor of Neanderthal man.

Some of its characteristic features are listed below: i. They had massive and heavily built jaws with moderate size teeth. ii. They lacked chin but had developed eye ridges. (There is another GAP of fossil record of around 50,000 years)

6. Neanderthal Man (Homo sapiens neanderthalensis) They are considered a primitive form of modern man that thrived in Europe, Asia and North America between 1,00,000 - 40,000 years ago. Fossils of Neanderthal man were recovered from Neanderthal Valley (Germany) from the late Pleistocene epoch by Carl Fuhlott. Later many other fossils were excavated in various parts of the world by different palaeontologists. It is considered that H. sapiens neanderthalensis did not evolve into H. sapiens, which implies they might have vanished due to extreme cold weather.

Some of its characteristic features are listed below: i. They were like modern men with tallness of around 5 feet and faces projecting slightly forward. ii. They walked upright and had low brows, receding jaws, and high domed heads. iii. Their cranial capacity was 1400 c.c. like a modern man. iv. Neanderthals were cave dwellers, skilled hunters (all time predators) and were adapted to a cold environment and harsh climate. They had fashioned the skin into clothing. v. They were omnivorous and cannibals. vi. They used to light fire in natural caves at night for heat and light. vii. It is believed that they buried their dead with flowers and tools. And they may have religion.
Figure: 7.4.9 Neanderthal man (skull, face) and stone tool

7. Cro-Magnon man (Homo sapiens fossilis). They are considered the early form of modern humans that thrived around 34,000 years ago in the Holocene epoch. They were more developed than Neanderthalman. Their fossils were first discovered in 1868 from Cro-Magnon rocks of France by Mac Gregor. Thus, they are called Cro- Magnon man. Thus, it is regarded as the most recent ancestor of modern man. It became extinct about 10,000-11,000 years ago.
